safety.statement: Each endpoint has exactly one authoritative active epoch.
Accepted epoch numbers never decrease during normal protocol execution.
Candidate or pending keys cannot authorize normal commands.
Cryptographic completion and operational SDLS activation are distinct state transitions.
Replayed identifiers and non-forward commit or confirmation epochs are rejected.
After VERIFIED, compromised key references cannot authenticate accepted commands.
Conflicting epochs cannot be simultaneously authoritative at one endpoint.
Recovery messages bind spacecraft identity, recovery ID, epoch information, counter, transcript, authority, and candidate reference when present.
Pending states, activation receipts, retries, and lifetimes are bounded.
No automatic fallback to a prior compromised epoch is permitted.
The ground cannot select a target using simulator-only spacecraft state.
An exact commit retry may re-emit confirmation but cannot activate the spacecraft twice.
A recovery-authority counter never decreases and equal counters are accepted only for an exact pending retry.

liveness.statement: Under a finite passive interval and bounded delivery, a recoverable treatment terminates in an explicit outcome.
No protocol receives a liveness claim against indefinite suppression.
Retry cannot reopen stale, conflicting, or replayed state.
Within the configured transmission budget, one lost prepare, response, commit, or confirmation can be retried without allocating an unbounded state set.

evidence.statement: Every state-changing transition produces an append-only event.
SUCCESS requires endpoint convergence and complete command/status verification evidence.
Loss of status telemetry after endpoint convergence produces INDETERMINATE, not cryptographic divergence.
Ordering uses simulator event sequence, not wall-clock timestamps.
SECURE_DEGRADED records incomplete operational restoration and cannot be reported as SUCCESS.

baseline_expectations.statement: B0 cannot claim PCS after compromise of the OTAR-protecting master key.
B1 requires party-specific transcript completion and mandatory key confirmation.
The primary B1 policy activates each endpoint on local completion; final-confirmation loss therefore produces G_AHEAD and DIVERGED.
The status-gated B1 variant adds an explicit fourth message and must model status loss as S_AHEAD and DIVERGED.
No B1 policy may use simulator-wide bilateral-delivery knowledge as an activation guard.
B2 is the Poettering-Roesler URKE state-evolution pattern adapted as a ground-to-space strict baseline.
Traffic-key reveal and sender-state or receiver-state exposure are distinct compromise scopes.
A fresh update may replace an exposed traffic key without implying recovery from receiver-state exposure.
Passive sender-state exposure can recover only while copied state is not used to desynchronize the receiver.
In-sync receiver-state exposure makes later aligned keys attacker-traceable in the strict URKE model.
A dropped update after sender evolution can permanently lock the strict baseline because no prior state or recovery checkpoint is retained.

provisional_treatment_expectations.statement: Ground proposes an epoch floor using only ground state and the external recovery-authority floor; spacecraft selects the exact forward target.
RECOVERY_PREPARE and RECOVERY_RESPONSE cannot authorize normal commands.
Spacecraft activates on an exact commit and ground activates on an exact confirmation.
One exact commit retry can use a bounded activation receipt to recover from confirmation loss without second activation.
Confirmation-budget exhaustion after spacecraft activation is SECURE_DEGRADED unless no authorized recovery path remains.
All T1 outcome oracles remain provisional until independent cryptography review.
